title: Supply curve inference playbook — concurrency vs unit cost
summary: Sketch of a practical supply-curve framing for inference capacity decisions: how per-concurrency unit cost and p99 latency evolve as we allocate more simultaneous sessions/slots. Intended to be a short, actionable internal brief (bench notes + lightweight ascii charts) to guide console knobs and Dedicated capacity sizing.
findings: We observe a concave supply curve: marginal cost per additional QPS increases slowly at low concurrency, then accelerates as memory and kernel saturation appear.
p99 latency remains flat through the first knee (about 30-40 concurrent sessions for rtx-like instances) but degrades rapidly after the second knee when swapping / slow-paths trigger.
Small increases in allowed concurrency (5-15%) can yield large throughput benefits at modest cost until the first knee; beyond that point, batching & kv-cache optimization become critical.
Different model families show different knee locations; quantized variants shift the knees right (higher concurrency) but slightly raise per-token CPU overhead for decoding paths.
Autoscaling step sizes that jump across knee points cause disproportionate p99 spikes; smoothing changes or staging can mitigate that.
A 'slot price' derived from marginal cost is a useful internal metric to expose to Console tooling for routing and capacity recommendations.

Supply curve interpretation: low-concurrency region (0-30) = efficient, cost slow-growth; mid region (30-50) = onset of tail risk; high region (50+) = exponential cost ramp and p99 blowup.

Marginal cost per additional slot (illustrative):
- 0->10: +0.08 $/QPS
- 10->30: +0.015 $/QPS per slot (economies of batching)
- 30->50: +0.09 $/QPS per slot (cache pressure)
- 50->100: +0.6 $/QPS per slot (slow-path, swapping)
methodology: Short test harness notes: run on a Dedicated-like cluster (4x A100 40GB-equivalent nodes) under synthetic sessionized workload. Models: llama-2-13b translated to inference shims (fp16), plus a 4-bit quantized variant. Input mix: 70% short-turn (<=64 tokens), 30% long-turn (avg 512 tokens), arrival Poisson with bursts emulated via superposed Poisson. Metrics: cost per QPS estimated from measured GPU-hours + amortized infra + slot allocation overhead; p50/p95/p99 latency measured at client-observed tail. Run window: 30m steady plus 15m ramp up/down. Notes: trials labeled by concurrency cap and prewarm policy. All numbers are approximate and environment-dependent.
recommended_actions: Expose a 'marginal slot price' in Console that updates per model and region — use it to recommend default concurrency caps for new tenants.
Implement a smoothing policy for autoscaler that avoids jumps across observed knee points (e.g., incremental steps <=10% or staged capacity add).
Bundle quantized model options in 'high-concurrency' templates with explicit caveats on p50/p99 shifts; recommend batching heuristics tuned to token-length mix.
Add an observability panel: supply-curve heatmap (concurrency on x, cost on y, p99 overlay) per model-family to help sales/solutions sizing calls.
Run a longer-duration soak (24h) on a mixed production trace to confirm spot-knee locations under real arrival correlations before locking defaults.
